crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Thematic Coding
children.blurb: Thematic coding is a qualitative analysis technique for identifying, organising and interpreting patterns of meaning in text, interview transcripts, field notes and other unstructured material.

children.name: Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation
children.blurb: Interview transcription and speaker separation in qualitative analysis and mixed methods refers to converting recorded interviews, focus groups, and multi-party conversations into text while attributing each utterance to the correct participant.

children.name: Finding Patterns in Lived Experience
children.blurb: Finding patterns in lived experience refers to systematic analysis of qualitative data such as interviews, diaries, open-ended survey responses, and field notes to identify recurring themes, narratives, and meanings.

children.name: Ethnographic Synthesis
children.blurb: Ethnographic synthesis brings together findings from multiple ethnographic studies to build higher-order interpretations of cultural and social phenomena.

children.name: Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data
children.blurb: Combining qualitative and quantitative data means bringing together non-numeric evidence such as interviews, field notes, documents, or open-ended survey responses with numeric measures, counts, or model outputs.

sections.body: This field is where artificial intelligence is applied to non-numeric research material, interviews, field notes, open ended survey answers, and documents. Right now AI is doing actual work in thematic coding by clustering similar phrases and suggesting code labels, in transcription by converting audio to text and separating multiple speakers, and in pattern finding by surfacing recurring ideas across large sets of lived experience accounts. Ethnographic synthesis uses these tools to pull together observations from different sites or groups, and mixed methods work uses AI to connect qualitative themes with quantitative measures. The pages under this section describe those concrete tasks rather than theoretical possibilities.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Transcription and speaker separation are the most mature, with reliable results for clear audio and a small number of speakers, but they still struggle with heavy accents, overlapping speech, and background noise. Thematic coding tools can propose codes and group text, yet a researcher must still read, rename, and merge codes because the tools miss context and irony. Pattern finding in lived experience works well for surface level repetition but not for subtle or contradictory meanings. Ethnographic synthesis remains largely human led, with AI assisting in retrieval and comparison rather than producing trustworthy interpretation. Combining qualitative and quantitative data is still an open problem, because current tools can align themes with numbers but cannot yet explain why a pattern exists. Across the 135 research papers held in this library, the honest limit is that these systems support analysis, they do not replace judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader starting with Thematic Coding will see how AI proposes and organizes codes from text. Interview Transcription and Speaker Separation covers the earlier step of turning recorded talk into usable text and who said what. Finding Patterns in Lived Experience moves from coded text to broader recurring ideas across many participants. Ethnographic Synthesis then shows how those patterns are brought together across sites, times, or cultural settings. Finally, Combining Qualitative and Quantitative Data addresses the harder task of linking those qualitative findings to numerical results in a single study. Together the pages follow the workflow from raw audio to integrated analysis.
